explanation_en: Literally 'to create noise,' this expression is widely used in political, corporate, and media contexts to mean causing friction, misunderstandings, or unnecessary complications. 'Ruído' refers to any interference that disrupts smooth communication or relations. It is an excellent B2/C1 collocation for describing diplomatic tension or public relations issues.

examples.en_text: The lack of clear communication between departments always creates unnecessary friction.
examples.target_text: A falta de comunicação clara entre os departamentos sempre cria ruídos desnecessários.

examples.en_text: Talking about money during dinner usually causes friction in the family.
examples.target_text: Falar sobre dinheiro durante o jantar costuma criar ruídos na família.

examples.en_text: The management's new decision caused friction among the employees.
examples.target_text: A nova decisão da gerência criou ruídos entre os funcionários.

examples.en_text: That post on social media ended up causing friction in their relationship.
examples.target_text: Aquela publicação nas redes sociais acabou por criar ruídos na relação deles.

examples.en_text: Changing the project rules halfway through will only create friction in the group.
examples.target_text: Mudar as regras do projeto a meio do caminho só vai criar ruídos no grupo.

examples.en_text: I prefer to be direct to avoid any misunderstanding that might cause friction between us.
examples.target_text: Eu prefiro ser direto para evitar qualquer mal-entendido que crie ruídos entre nós.

explanation_en: This phrase refers to a pre-arranged agreement, setup, or collusion between parties who pretend to be acting independently or even in opposition. It is equivalent to 'inside job' or 'collusion' in English. It is commonly used in political analysis, sports, and investigative journalism to describe situations that are not as spontaneous as they appear.

examples.en_text: I thought the job interview was a pre-arranged setup to hire the director's cousin.
examples.target_text: Eu achei que a entrevista de emprego foi um jogo combinado para contratar o primo do diretor.

examples.en_text: That television debate seemed like a pre-arranged setup between the two candidates.
examples.target_text: Aquele debate na televisão parecia um jogo combinado entre os dois candidatos.

examples.en_text: I'm not going to participate in this auction because I'm sure it's a rigged setup.
examples.target_text: Não vou participar desse leilão porque tenho certeza de que é jogo combinado.

examples.en_text: The police are investigating the championship result due to suspicion of a fixed match.
examples.target_text: A polícia está investigando o resultado do campeonato por suspeita de jogo combinado.

examples.en_text: We lost the board game because they made a secret pre-arranged deal.
examples.target_text: Nós perdemos o jogo de tabuleiro porque eles fizeram um jogo combinado em segredo.

examples.en_text: There's no point in competing for this prize, everyone knows it's a setup.
examples.target_text: Não adianta concorrer a esse prêmio, todo mundo sabe que isso é jogo combinado.

explanation_en: This is a metaphorical expression meaning to celebrate a victory or success, often used in the negative ('não se deve abrir...') to warn against celebrating prematurely. It is the Portuguese equivalent of 'don't pop the champagne yet.' It is highly idiomatic and adds a vivid, native-like touch to discussions about ongoing events or uncertain outcomes.

examples.en_text: Don't celebrate before the final whistle; it's still too early to celebrate prematurely.
examples.target_text: Não comemore antes do apito final; ainda é cedo para abrir garrafas de champanhe.

examples.en_text: They thought the contract was guaranteed and were already celebrating prematurely, but the client changed their mind.
examples.target_text: Eles achavam que o contrato estava garantido e já estavam abrindo garrafas de champanhe, mas o cliente mudou de ideia.

examples.en_text: The candidate started celebrating prematurely before all the votes were counted and ended up losing.
examples.target_text: O candidato começou a abrir garrafas de champanhe antes de apurar todos os votos e acabou perdendo.

examples.en_text: Just because the exam went well, don't start celebrating prematurely; we still need to know the grade.
examples.target_text: Só porque a prova correu bem, não comece já a abrir garrafas de champanhe; ainda falta saber a nota.

examples.en_text: We haven't signed the agreement yet, so it's better not to celebrate prematurely.
examples.target_text: Nós ainda não assinamos o acordo, por isso é melhor não abrir garrafas de champanhe antes do tempo.

examples.en_text: The investor was already celebrating prematurely with the rise of the shares, but the next day the market fell.
examples.target_text: O investidor já estava abrindo garrafas de champanhe com a subida das ações, mas no dia seguinte o mercado caiu.

explanation_en: Literally 'quicksand' or 'shifting ground,' this metaphor is used to describe an unstable, risky, or highly unpredictable situation where one must tread carefully. It is often used in political and economic commentary to describe a delicate state of affairs where things can easily go wrong. It is a sophisticated B2/C1 expression that elevates a learner's descriptive vocabulary.

examples.en_text: Talking about politics at the dinner table is always entering risky territory.
examples.target_text: Falar sobre política na mesa de jantar é sempre entrar em terreno movediço.

examples.en_text: Investing all your money in this new company is stepping on unstable ground.
examples.target_text: Investir todo o teu dinheiro nesta nova empresa é pisar em terreno movediço.

examples.en_text: When the boss started asking questions about the project, I realized I was on shaky ground.
examples.target_text: Quando o chefe começou a fazer perguntas sobre o projeto, percebi que estava em terreno movediço.

examples.en_text: Without a signed contract, our partnership is on unstable ground.
examples.target_text: Sem um contrato assinado, a nossa parceria está num terreno movediço.

examples.en_text: I prefer not to give advice on other people's marriages; it's very risky territory.
examples.target_text: Eu prefiro não dar conselhos sobre casamentos alheios, é um terreno muito movediço.

examples.en_text: Changing the rules of the game halfway through the championship puts the organization on shaky ground.
examples.target_text: Mudar as regras do jogo a meio do campeonato coloca a organização num terreno movediço.

explanation_en: This idiomatic expression means to get something exactly right, to hit the mark, or to find the perfect balance/dosage in an action. It originates from cooking (getting the ingredients or seasoning just right) but is widely used in abstract contexts like politics, art, and decision-making. It is a great alternative to the more basic 'fazer bem' or 'acertar.'

examples.en_text: After trying several times, I finally got the cake recipe right.
examples.target_text: Depois de tentar várias vezes, finalmente acertei a mão na receita de bolo.

examples.en_text: In the beginning it's hard to use this tool, but soon you'll get the hang of it.
examples.target_text: No começo é difícil usar essa ferramenta, mas logo você acerta a mão.

examples.en_text: The painter hasn't yet got the right shade of blue that the client asked for.
examples.target_text: O pintor ainda não acertou a mão no tom de azul que o cliente pediu.

examples.en_text: It's hard to get the right amount of water for these plants.
examples.target_text: É difícil acertar a mão na quantidade de água para essas plantas.

examples.en_text: It took the company a while to hit the mark with the marketing campaign, but now sales have gone up.
examples.target_text: A empresa demorou para acertar a mão na campanha de marketing, mas agora as vendas subiram.

examples.en_text: She practiced a lot and finally got the rhythm of the song right.
examples.target_text: Ela treinou bastante e finalmente acertou a mão no ritmo da música.

explanation_en: This highly expressive idiom literally translates to 'even the stones know,' meaning that a fact is extremely obvious, widely known, and indisputable. It is used to emphasize that there is no point in denying or hiding something because it is common knowledge. It is equivalent to the English 'everyone and their mother knows.'

examples.en_text: That they are dating in secret? Everyone already knows!
examples.target_text: Que eles estão namorando em segredo? Até as pedras já sabem!

examples.en_text: Everyone knows that the mayor is going to run for office again.
examples.target_text: Até as pedras sabem que o prefeito vai se candidatar novamente.

examples.en_text: There's no use trying to hide the mistake, everyone already knows what happened.
examples.target_text: Não adianta tentar esconder o erro, até as pedras já sabem o que aconteceu.

examples.en_text: She pretended to be surprised, but everyone knew about the party.
examples.target_text: Ela fingiu ficar surpresa, mas até as pedras sabiam da festa.

examples.en_text: Everyone knows that fuel prices are going to go up next week.
examples.target_text: Até as pedras sabem que os preços dos combustíveis vão subir na próxima semana.

examples.en_text: Who is going to win the championship? Everyone knows it will be our team.
examples.target_text: Quem vai ganhar o campeonato? Até as pedras sabem que será o nosso time.

explanation_en: The conjunction 'caso' (in case / if) triggers the present subjunctive ('fique') to express a hypothetical condition. It is a highly elegant and common alternative to 'se' (which would trigger the future subjunctive 'se ficar'). Advanced learners should master this pattern to sound more natural in formal writing and analytical speech.

examples.en_text: Should it become evident that the project will be delayed, we need to notify the client immediately.
examples.target_text: Caso fique evidente que o projeto vai atrasar, precisamos avisar o cliente imediatamente.

examples.en_text: Should it become evident that the situation is worsening, we should go to the hospital.
examples.target_text: Caso fique evidente que a situação está piorando, devemos ir ao hospital.

examples.en_text: Should it become evident that the students did not understand the material, the teacher will repeat the explanation.
examples.target_text: Caso fique evidente que os alunos não compreenderam a matéria, o professor vai repetir a explicação.

examples.en_text: Should it become evident that the company is making a loss, we will have to cut expenses.
examples.target_text: Caso fique evidente que a empresa está tendo prejuízo, teremos de cortar despesas.

examples.en_text: Should it become evident that the app has a security flaw, the team will release an update immediately.
examples.target_text: Caso fique evidente que o aplicativo tem uma falha de segurança, a equipe lançará uma atualização imediatamente.

examples.en_text: Should it become evident that it is going to rain, it is better for us to cancel the picnic in the park.
examples.target_text: Caso fique evidente que vai chover, é melhor cancelarmos o piquenique no parque.

explanation_en: Literally meaning 'the conversation is over', this colloquial expression is used to state that a matter is settled, indisputable, or has reached its absolute limit. It is highly effective in debates or informal arguments to shut down further speculation. It carries a decisive, sometimes blunt tone depending on the context.

examples.en_text: I already told you that you are going to bed now, and that's it!
examples.target_text: Já te disse que vais para a cama agora e acabou a conversa!

examples.en_text: We don't have money to buy a new car this year, so end of story.
examples.target_text: Não temos dinheiro para comprar um carro novo este ano, por isso acabou a conversa.

examples.en_text: The deadline is tomorrow at nine in the morning, and that's final.
examples.target_text: O prazo limite é amanhã às nove da manhã e acabou a conversa.

examples.en_text: I am not going to argue with you about this subject anymore, end of story.
examples.target_text: Eu não vou discutir mais contigo sobre este assunto, acabou a conversa.

examples.en_text: Today there are no sweets for anyone, and that's that.
examples.target_text: Hoje não há doces para ninguém e acabou a conversa.

examples.en_text: I decided that I am not going to that party, and that's it.
examples.target_text: Decidi que não vou àquela festa e acabou a conversa.

explanation_en: A formal political and geopolitical collocation meaning 'balance of power' or 'correlation of forces'. It is widely used in news, political analysis, and academic discussions in Portuguese to describe how power is distributed between opposing sides. Learners should note that 'correlação' is preferred over 'balanço' in this specific political context.

examples.en_text: With the opposition's victory, the balance of power in parliament changed completely.
examples.target_text: Com a vitória da oposição, a correlação de forças no parlamento mudou completamente.

examples.en_text: At the negotiation table, the balance of power was favorable to the workers.
examples.target_text: Na mesa de negociação, a correlação de forças era favorável aos trabalhadores.

examples.en_text: The creation of the new military alliance altered the balance of power in the region.
examples.target_text: A criação da nova aliança militar alterou a correlação de forças na região.

examples.en_text: The merger of the two large companies will change the balance of power in the technology market.
examples.target_text: A fusão das duas grandes empresas vai mudar a correlação de forças no mercado de tecnologia.

examples.en_text: Before making a decision, the coach analyzed the balance of power between the two teams.
examples.target_text: Antes de tomar uma decisão, o treinador analisou a correlação de forças entre os dois times.

examples.en_text: The street protests helped to balance the balance of power between the government and society.
examples.target_text: Os protestos de rua ajudaram a equilibrar a correlação de forças entre o governo e a sociedade.

explanation_en: Borrowed from boxing terminology (referring to the canvas ring mat), 'na lona' is an idiomatic expression meaning to be completely defeated, exhausted, or ruined. In everyday speech, it can describe someone who is broke, extremely tired, or a political actor who has lost all leverage. Here, it is used metaphorically to describe a total defeat.

examples.en_text: After running the marathon, I was completely exhausted.
examples.target_text: Depois de correr a maratona, eu estava completamente na lona.

examples.en_text: With the economic crisis, his small company was on the ropes.
examples.target_text: Com a crise econômica, a pequena empresa dele ficou na lona.

examples.en_text: This bad flu left me down for the count the whole week.
examples.target_text: Essa gripe forte me deixou na lona a semana inteira.

examples.en_text: After the breakup, he felt down in the dumps for a few months.
examples.target_text: Depois do fim do namoro, ele se sentiu na lona por alguns meses.

examples.en_text: I spent all my money on the trip and now I'm broke.
examples.target_text: Gastei todo o meu dinheiro na viagem e agora estou na lona.

examples.en_text: I worked twelve hours today and got home completely exhausted.
examples.target_text: Trabalhei doze horas hoje e cheguei em casa na lona.

explanation_en: A very common idiomatic collocation meaning 'to buy time' or 'to stall'. It is used in both everyday personal situations and high-level political or business negotiations. It is highly versatile and essential for B2/C1 learners to use instead of more literal, clunkier phrasing.

examples.en_text: I need to make up an excuse to buy time before the meeting.
examples.target_text: Eu preciso inventar uma desculpa para ganhar tempo antes da reunião.

examples.en_text: We tried to buy time while the boss hadn't arrived yet.
examples.target_text: Nós tentamos ganhar tempo enquanto o chefe não chegava.

examples.en_text: If we postpone the delivery, we will buy time to correct the mistakes.
examples.target_text: Se nós adiarmos a entrega, vamos ganhar tempo para corrigir os erros.

examples.en_text: He is just stalling because he hasn't made a decision yet.
examples.target_text: Ele está apenas ganhando tempo porque ainda não tomou uma decisão.

examples.en_text: Speak slowly so that we can buy time and think of a solution.
examples.target_text: Fale devagar para que possamos ganhar tempo e pensar em uma solução.

examples.en_text: With that vague answer, the politician bought time to prepare himself better.
examples.target_text: Com aquela resposta vaga, o político ganhou tempo para se preparar melhor.

explanation_en: The adjective 'acachapante' means crushing, overwhelming, or staggering (e.g., a crushing victory or defeat). Combined with 'de forma', it functions as an adverb meaning 'overwhelmingly'. This is a high-level (C1) vocabulary item that adds a strong, dramatic emphasis to descriptions of outcomes.

examples.en_text: The home team won the derby overwhelmingly by five to zero.
examples.target_text: O time da casa venceu o clássico de forma acachapante por cinco a zero.

examples.en_text: She won the mayoral election overwhelmingly, with more than 70% of the votes.
examples.target_text: Ela ganhou as eleições para prefeita de forma acachapante, com mais de 70% dos votos.

examples.en_text: The lawyer proved his client's innocence in a crushing manner during the trial.
examples.target_text: O advogado provou a inocência do seu cliente de forma acachapante durante o julgamento.

examples.en_text: The new cell phone brand overwhelmingly outperformed the competition in just a few months.
examples.target_text: A nova marca de celulares superou a concorrência de forma acachapante em poucos meses.

examples.en_text: The presented data overwhelmingly shows the impact of global warming.
examples.target_text: Os dados apresentados mostram de forma acachapante o impacto do aquecimento global.

examples.en_text: The young pianist overwhelmingly defeated the other contestants at the music festival.
examples.target_text: O jovem pianista derrotou os outros concorrentes de forma acachapante no festival de música.
